column3: It completes the immediate sequence: devils only cast stolen scraps of hearing, and most of what they relay is false.
The waste-versus-rightful-distribution channel concerns remote rebellion but adds little to barred access to hearing.
The son's isolation from Noah's saving company gives a concrete boundary parallel, though not one about access to revelation.
The stolen-hearing intruder is pursued by a visible flame, directly showing that unauthorized hearing is blocked and exposed.
The immediately preceding denial that devils brought the revelation supplies the source-side premise for their exclusion from hearing.
Allah's hearing and sight provide only a broad divine-hearing frame, not the exclusion of hostile carriers.
The promise of support for messengers does not clarify restricted access to the hearing source.
Calling squanderers brothers of devils gives the channel's rebellious-agent background but not the hearing restriction itself.
Allah's hearing and sight reassure Moses and Aaron but do not develop hostile exclusion from revelation.
Misleaders who turn others from the path parallel obstruction generally, without an access-to-hearing relation.
The adjacent assertion that devils neither ought nor are able to do it directly reinforces their incapacity before the stated exclusion.
Abraham's deliberate separation from idolatrous calling parallels withdrawal from a corrupt relation, but not barred hearing.
Being veiled from the Lord gives an eschatological counterpart to exclusion from a source of reception.
The warning against following Satan identifies hostile influence, while the channel link remains too indirect for the hearing barrier.
Temporary bodily separation is a limited boundary analogy and does not concern access to transmitted hearing.
Attentive hearing as conscious witnessing contrasts with the devils' excluded, fragmentary access.
Guarding the heaven from every expelled devil supplies the protective setting for the hearing restriction.
Dismissing a message as unheard in inherited tradition shows a closed hearing norm, distinct from the devils' enforced exclusion.
Hearing is a divinely granted faculty, which contrasts with hostile agents' lack of legitimate access to the source.
Seeking refuge from satanic provocation names the adversary but adds little to the specific restriction on hearing.
The granted faculties of hearing and reflection contrast with devils' illicit attempt to acquire and relay sound.
Moses' request for nonviolent separation gives a boundary parallel, though it lacks the focus's hearing-access claim.
Seeking refuge from stoning supplies only the conflict setting around the related separation channel.
Abraham's completed separation from idolaters shows a productive withdrawal, but not restricted reception.
Seeing the promised event as distant does not illuminate exclusion from hearing.
The harmful companion motif supplies only a remote rebellious-agent parallel.
Plausible speech conceals hostile opponents, which cautions against treating audible words as reliable transmission.
Oath-shielded obstruction of God's path is a broad hostile-action parallel only.
The absence of vain speech in Paradise concerns a purified sound environment, not barred access to revelation.
Noncombatant withdrawal is a legal separation analogy without a hearing relation.
Selling God's signs and blocking His path does not add to the devils' restricted hearing.
Satan's abandonment after diverting someone from remembrance gives a consequence of hostile influence, not the access barrier.
The future command to hear and see contrasts present refusal with unavoidable reception, though not covert intrusion.
Turning away from the reminder parallels refusing its hearing, but differs from being forcibly excluded.
The deceiver's misleading role supplies only a distant channel association.
The jinn's open hearing of the Quran offers a lawful, responsive contrast to the hostile agents barred from the hearing field.
Believers' turning from vain speech concerns selective conduct, not access to the source.
Noah's disavowal of others' crimes gives a separation motif but does not clarify hearing restriction.
Refuge from satanic provocation names the same adversarial pressure without adding to source exclusion.
Neglect of prayer is not materially connected to restricted hearing.
Abandoning the Quran describes failed reception among people, contrasting with the devils' barred access.
The majority turn away so as not to hear, a human refusal that sharply contrasts with the devils' inability to hear.
Moses is commanded to listen to revelation, supplying the positive, authorized counterpart to excluded hostile listeners.
Hearing Hell's roar concerns judgmental sound, not access to the revelation source.
Allah's choice of angelic and human messengers gives broad authority for true transmission but no hearing barrier.
The devils cannot listen to the exalted assembly and are pelted away, closely paralleling the focus's exclusion from hearing.
Satan's enmity explains the hostile role but adds no detail about hearing access.
Paradise's freedom from idle speech is a distant sound-environment parallel.
Former listening posts are now guarded by flames, directly depicting the enforced end of covert hearing access.
Noah's refusal to drive believers away concerns social exclusion rather than hearing.
Leaving a gathering that mocks revelation regulates human participation after hearing, not access to its source.
Opponents hear the reminder yet respond with abuse, distinguishing hostile reception from truthful understanding.
The wind and resurrection image does not clarify restricted hearing.
Rejecting a message because ancestors never heard it shows a closed inherited hearing frame, but not the focus's barrier.
The damned not hearing in Hell is an eschatological deprivation without the covert-access setting.
The condemned admit that receptive hearing and reasoning would have prevented ruin, contrasting with hostile misuse of hearing.
A turned-away deaf audience cannot be made to hear the call, paralleling failed reception rather than barred intrusion.
Dawn repentance does not add to understanding the hearing exclusion.
Allah's hearing and knowledge underwrite trust in a truce but add little to the focus's source restriction.
The call to listen is a general imperative without an access boundary.
The silence of destroyed generations is a remote auditory contrast only.
Abraham asks whether idols hear their callers, contrasting powerless recipients with the guarded true source.
Responsible treatment of heard reports contrasts with the devils' false relay, though it is a human ethical case.
Hearing, sight, and heart are accountable faculties, underscoring why reliable reception cannot be assumed from mere access.
Hearing recited signs while persisting arrogantly separates physical audition from receptive hearing, relevant to the focus's restricted field.
The claim that corrupters do not perceive does not add a distinct hearing or exclusion relation.
We hear and obey gives the positive endpoint of authorized hearing, contrasting with deceptive hostile transmission.
Divine ownership of hearing and sight gives only broad authority behind the guarded source.
The absence of idle speech in Paradise is a remote contrast to false utterance.
Those who say they hear while not truly hearing distinguish sound reception from responsive hearing, clarifying the focus's hearing language.
The challenge to produce proof from any claimed listening route directly contests unauthorized access to hidden information.
The condemned were unable to hear or see, an incapacity parallel but outside the focus's covert-listener scene.
People listen but retain nothing because their hearts are sealed, contrasting audible exposure with meaningful reception.
Created hearing and sight supply a general faculty frame already established by earlier cards.
Hearing witnessing against its owner concerns accountability, not access to revelation.
Twisting speech while claiming to hear shows corrupt verbal reception, though it does not establish the guarded source.
Opponents listen in order to construct hostile private speech, showing that hearing access can be used for distortion rather than guidance.
The bare reference to criminals adds no usable connection.
The jinn recognize a heard book as confirming truth and guiding rightly, a positive contrast to false fragmentary relay.
Allah as the Hearing, Knowing one grounds the surrounding revelation sequence, though the focus states the exclusion more directly.
False objects cannot hear calls or respond even if they did, offering a detailed incapacity contrast to claims of access and relay.
The created faculties of hearing, sight, and hearts repeat a broad background already supplied by stronger candidates.
Allah's hearing and sight affirm comprehensive awareness but not a restriction on hostile listeners.
The opponents' plotting adds only a general hostile-agent motif.
Human hearing and sight as testing faculties are too general after earlier faculty cards.
Expectation of meeting the Lord does not clarify restricted hearing.
The future summons to listen is an auditory command without the focus's barrier or false relay.
Failed hypocritical claims and wasted works do not add to hearing exclusion.
Hearing the final cry concerns eschatological compulsion, not access to revelation.
Messengerly relief after despair has no material connection to restricted hearing.
Following the messenger and revealed light gives broad guidance but no distinct hearing-access point.
The prophet cannot make the deaf hear, a direct incapacity parallel that remains different from excluding covert intruders.
Noah's public call gives only the setting of an offered message and does not develop hearing reception.
Destruction for earnings does not clarify hearing or exclusion.
Denial of the Hour and divine knowledge of the unseen do not add to the focus's hearing relation.
False claims of revelation and arrogance toward signs parallel deceptive speech, but not barred access to hearing.
Eager listening to lies and alteration of words closely parallels unreliable relay, though it is not the guarded-source scene.
The decree against Noah's wrongdoers does not add to restricted hearing.
Hearing a social plot has no material connection to the focus.
Inheritance shares do not clarify the hearing exclusion.
The question immediately introduces the class of people upon whom devils descend, supplying the lead-in to the focus's account of their barred hearing.
Devils descend upon every sinful liar, identifying the deceptive human recipients who receive the fragments described after the focus.
The eavesdroppers are explicitly repelled and assigned lasting punishment, reinforcing that their exclusion from the heavenly hearing field is enforced.
Even one who snatches a fragment of hearing is pursued by a piercing flame, directly matching illicit acquisition and its consequence.
The jinn find the heaven filled with strong guards and flames, providing the guarded architecture behind their inability to listen.
The Knower of the unseen does not disclose it freely, establishing the source-side restriction that prevents unauthorized acquisition.
A chosen messenger is the stated exception, and guards are sent before and behind him, sharply distinguishing authorized revelation from devilish access.
The guarding of the messenger's conveyed message confirms that transmitted revelation is encompassed and counted, not open to hostile interception.
The Quran is expressly denied to be the word of an accursed devil, directly excluding the rival carrier claim behind the focus.
Naming it the word conveyed by a noble messenger supplies the positive authorized carrier contrast to devils barred from hearing.
The messenger is not withholding the unseen, contrasting trustworthy disclosure with the devils' inaccessible, fragmentary claims.
The revelation is explicitly not the word of a poet, excluding a competing human source alongside the focus's devilish alternative.
It is likewise not the word of a soothsayer, directly narrowing false claims to hidden-message access.
The Trustworthy Spirit brings the revelation down, supplying the authorized bearer that contrasts with devils unable to descend with it.
Revelation placed upon the Prophet's heart identifies its protected destination, rather than an accessible hearing field for rival carriers.
Its clear Arabic delivery describes the public, intelligible form of the protected revelation after its authorized descent.
Human and jinn devils inspire one another with embellished deceptive speech, giving a broader account of the false relay opposed to guarded revelation.
Devils inspire their allies to dispute, showing a terrestrial route of hostile verbal influence distinct from legitimate revelation.
Satan may cast into recitation, but Allah abolishes that casting and perfects His signs, directly establishing protection against corrupt intrusion.
The devils' teaching of harmful magic shows another false knowledge-transmission route, contrasting with the protected revelatory source.
The jinn do not know the unseen, directly undermining any claim that they possess independent access to hidden information.
Allah's promise to preserve the Reminder supplies the broader protection principle underlying the exclusion of hostile listeners.
Allah's revelation reaches humans only by specified divine modes or through a sent messenger, delimiting legitimate access and transmission.
The Spirit descends with revelation upon those Allah chooses, adding an authorized-descent contrast to devilish non-descent.
Gabriel brings the Quran down to the Prophet's heart by Allah's permission, a close authorized-carrier counterpart.
The Quran is sent down with truth and as a bearer of good news and warning, distinguishing its source and purpose from false relay.
Falsehood cannot approach the Book from before or behind, broadening the focus's guarded-hearing claim into textual inviolability.
The Prophet denies independent possession of the unseen and follows only revelation, contrasting prophetic authorization with claims of covert access.
The Prophet's stated lack of independent unseen knowledge locates hidden knowledge with Allah rather than hostile or human carriers.
None in the heavens and earth knows the unseen except Allah, giving the comprehensive boundary behind the devils' restricted hearing.
